ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A certain current balance can be used to measure the magnitude of the magnetic induction in a uniform magnetic field, as shown in the figure. The right arm of the balance suspends a rectangular coil with $n=10$ turns and a horizontal side length of $l=10\mathrm{cm}$. The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field, with the direction of the magnetic induction perpendicular to the plane of the coil and pointing outward. When a current of $I=0.1\mathrm{A}$ flows through the coil in a clockwise direction, the balance is adjusted by adding weights until equilibrium is achieved. At this point, the mass of the weight in the left pan is $m_{1}=0.4\mathrm{kg}$, and the mass of the weight in the right pan is $m_{2}=0.5\mathrm{kg}$. The mass of the fine wire suspending the rectangular coil and the mass of the coil itself are negligible, and the acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

1. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction strength of the magnetic field at the location of the coil?
2. If only the current in the coil is reversed, how much mass needs to be added to the left pan to balance the arms of the scale again?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an equal-arm balance; weights are placed on the left pan, and weights are also placed on the right pan; below the right pan a rectangular coil is also suspended with a thin string. The lower part of the coil is in the magnetic-field region outlined by a blue dashed box, and inside the dashed box black dots indicate that the direction of the magnetic induction intensity is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. On the left and right vertical sides of the rectangular coil, the current directions are respectively marked: the current on the left side is upward, and the current on the right side is downward, indicating that the coil current is in the clockwise direction; the length of the horizontal side of the coil in the magnetic field is marked as l. From the structure shown in the figure it can be known that what produces a vertical influence on the balance is the horizontal wire segment in the magnetic field; the magnetic forces on the left and right vertical segments are in the horizontal direction and cancel each other, not changing the vertical balance of the balance. Reasoning: The magnetic-field direction is outward, and when the current in the coil is clockwise, the current direction of the lower horizontal side in the magnetic field corresponds to an upward magnetic force, so the magnitude of the vertically upward ampere force of the magnetic field on the n-turn coil is F=nBIl. The effective downward acting force of the right pan is m2g-F. When the equal-arm balance is balanced, there is m1g=m2g-nBIl, so nBIl=(m2-m1)g, B=(m2-m1)g/(nIl). Substituting m2-m1=0.5-0.4=0.10 kg, n=10, I=0.1 A, l=10 cm=0.10 m, and taking g≈10 N/kg, gives B=0.10×10/(10×0.1×0.10)=10 T. If only the coil current is reversed, then the ampere-force direction becomes downward, with unchanged magnitude, still equivalent to the gravity of 0.10 kg. At this time the total equivalent mass on the right side is m2+0.10 kg=0.5+0.1=0.6 kg. The left pan originally has 0.4 kg, so it is still necessary to add 0.6-0.4=0.2 kg.
